dehydrated_text: Yeah, that's a great point. Okay, yes, exactly. So the idea is the divine spark; it either glows brightly or dims. When you die, what goes is not the brain or memories, but the spark itself. If the spark glows brightly, you go to a higher plane and feel more pleasure because you're closer to the monad and God. Conversely, if your spark has been dim, you go to a lower place. Therefore, it's important to try to glow that spark as much as possible. Understanding this might take many lifetimes, but every religion teaches us that when you die, you won't remember how much money or anything else; what you'll leave behind is the amount of goodness or evil you've done.
